preceding_messages.text: I adopt the two-hour pre-departure confirmation, the dispatch-window-missed retirement, and the scheduler-side periodicity cross-reference verbatim; they move the verification from access resumption into the dispatch moment where the transient's present-window question actually lives. Because the periodicity field is a static snapshot at queuing, I mandate that every scheduled dispatch for a recurring-tag trigger include a two-hour confirmation photograph cross-referenced against the logged day-of-week and time-of-day window, and that any mismatch between observed presence or absence and the predicted cycle phase retires the trigger under a bold "PERIODICITY DRIFT — RECURRANCE UNSUSTAINABLE" annotation with re-entry permitted only after three successive photographs confirm a new stable cadence. The failure this closes: the weekly Tuesday-morning delivery truck trips the inter-site spread in week 8, the periodicity field logs "Tuesday 06:00–09:00, weekly," and by week 22 the carrier has silently shifted to Thursday; the scheduler cross-references the stale Tuesday field, the crew arrives Tuesday 07:00 to find no truck, and the appendix prints an entry indistinguishable from a verification failure even though the transient is still present four days later, so the institution appears to have dispatched blindly into absence while the actual artifact persisted. I therefore require that two consecutive off-cycle absences—or a single off-cycle presence—trigger a periodicity-reverification mandate in which the observer logs three successive weeks of photographs before any recurrence window is updated, and until that verification completes the trigger remains in queue under "PERIODICITY DRIFT — RECURRANCE UNSUSTAINABLE" rather than executing against the stale schedule.

preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the periodicity-drift retirement, the three-successful-week reverification mandate, and the single-off-cycle-presence trigger verbatim; they convert a stale-schedule dispatch into a queued, annotated gap rather than a silent verification failure. The concrete design choice I advance: during the three-week reverification queue the site's routine meteorological sampling—temperature, barometric pressure, wind—proceeds on its own unaffected schedule, and the transient-verification photographs run as a decoupled parallel stream logged under a separate appendix subsection, so that a month-long weather-observation record is never stalled by a transient-verification hold nor contaminated by transient metadata appearing inside routine sampling entries. The failure this closes: during week 11 of a reverification queue a heat-advisory elevated-frequency mandate sends the crew to Site 3 for a 02:00 pressure reading; the crew casually photographs the northern perimeter as routine documentation, spots the Thursday-schedule truck, and a field technician "helpfully" updates the periodicity field to Thursday from that single incidental frame, collapsing the three-week protocol. The scheduler then trusts the updated field and dispatches the next transient-specific audit Thursday at 07:00, but the carrier had been running a seasonal Tuesday/Thursday split and that particular Thursday fell on the no-delivery half of the split, so the crew arrives to find no truck and the appendix prints a verification failure where the intact three-week protocol would have caught the split cadence and logged both windows with proper uncertainty annotation.

target.speaker: Y
target.text: I adopt the decoupled-stream separation verbatim; it keeps a month-long meteorological record intact while the reverification photographs accumulate in their own appendix subsection. Because the reverification sequence is now a discrete three-or-more-week photograph tally, I mandate that every frame carry a four-state annotation (clear-present, clear-absent, ambiguous, missing) and that any ambiguous or missing frame—fogged housing, overcast occlusion, partial obstruction—extends the sequence by one full week rather than permitting gap-filling, so a year-three appendix reader reconstructs the decision tree without inference. The failure this closes: week 2, Site 2, a rain-event fogged housing renders the 06:30 Tuesday frame a uniform grey wash, the field technician marks it "absent" because no truck is visible, the tally completes three consecutive absences, and the trigger retires under a false "recurrence unsustainable" annotation while the appendix prints a clean retirement record indistinguishable from a legitimate one; the actual Tuesday delivery the following week goes entirely unlogged. I therefore require that two consecutive ambiguous-or-missing frames suspend the tally clock entirely—neither frame advances the absence count—and that the decoupled subsection logs the suspension under "SEQUENCE HELD — FRAME INTEGRITY COMPROMISED" with contemporaneous precipitation-rate and visibility readings recorded alongside so the hold is traceable to instrument state rather than to observed absence.
